label: prf:fibre-functor-atlas
title: Proof of fibre functor atlas
html:
Proof. (1) A fibre functor \tau' assigns to each object X in \mathbf{C} an R-module \tau'(X) and to each morphism f a linear map \tau'(f), preserving the tensor product. This is a concrete coordinate system for the abstract category — an affine chart.

(2) By the Tannaka–Krein theorem (\mathrm{SU}(2) emergence), any monoidal natural isomorphism \eta \colon \tau' \xrightarrow{\sim} \tau'' is determined by an element g \in G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) acting on the fibre. The set of all such isomorphisms is a principal homogeneous space for G — a G-torsor.

(3) If \eta_{01} \colon \tau' \to \tau'' and \eta_{12} \colon \tau'' \to \tau''' are monoidal natural isomorphisms, their composition \eta_{12} \circ \eta_{01} is the unique monoidal natural isomorphism \tau' \to \tau''' corresponding to the group product g_{12} \cdot g_{01}. The cocycle identity g_{02} = g_{12} \cdot g_{01} is the associativity of composition in the functor category.

(4) Connectedness: any two fibre functors are isomorphic (Tannaka–Krein). Simple transitivity: the isomorphism is unique up to G. \square
